tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use when...'), focuses on user intent (cost, spend, pricing, billing, savings, reservations, right-sizing, idle resources, etc.), explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the user may not name the domain directly (e.g., 'an investigation surfaces idle or oversized media resources'), and also clarifies scope boundaries (not for fault/outage investigation or general AWS cost review). It is a dense but reasonably concise paragraph appropriate for the breadth of services covered.
tests.evidence: Use when a customer asks about cost, spend, pricing, billing, savings, reservations, right-sizing, idle resources, start/stop scheduling, over-provisioned input specifications, channel class, or whether MediaConnect Router would be cheaper than flows. Also use when an investigation surfaces idle or oversized media resources.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific procedures (pricing API calls, CLI commands, service codes, thresholds) without explaining generic concepts the agent already knows. It assumes AWS/CLI familiarity and focuses entirely on Media Services-specific facts and procedures.
tests.evidence: Service codes: `AWSElementalMediaLive`, `AWSElementalMediaPackage`, `AWSElementalMediaTailor`, `AmazonCloudFront`, and `AWSMediaConnect` (candidate; if `describe-services` returns nothing for it, page through...)

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed per-service lookup tables (metric thresholds, field maps, lever lists) are offloaded to references/ files and only summarized or linked in the body; the body retains procedural steps and short illustrative tables (e.g., the presence-metric table, threshold gate table) which are reasonably concise and not raw reference dumps.
tests.evidence: - [references/medialive-cost-levers.md](references/medialive-cost-levers.md): reservations and break-even math, stop scheduling, channel class downgrade, idle push inputs, output ladder right-sizing.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All eight files in references/ are linked with markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by context specifying when/why to load it, e.g., tied to specific steps or conditions (validation rules, service-specific levers, field mapping needs).
tests.evidence: Apply the validation rules in section 5 of [references/pricing-data-acquisition.md](references/pricing-data-acquisition.md). USD only, non-negative decimals, tier ranges preserved, publication date captured.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal patterns.
tests.evidence: [references/data-transfer-map.md](references/data-transfer-map.md): which inter-service legs are free and which are charged

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (pricing acquisition, threshold gates, report structure) are prescribed exactly, while flexible judgment areas (which levers to evaluate, how to phrase questions to customer) leave room for agent discretion with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: Do not emit a recommendation that fails its gate. These gates encode where the math stops favoring the change; below them, the recommendation would cost the customer money or resilience.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When presenting alternatives (e.g., Price List Query API vs Bulk API), the skill designates a clear default and frames the alternative as a fallback only used when the primary is unavailable.
tests.evidence: If the `pricing:` actions are not granted, do not estimate rates from memory. The same data is published without credentials by the Price List Bulk API...

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable, repeatable methodology (acquire pricing, inventory resources, estimate usage, check coherence, evaluate levers, gate, report, validate) applicable to any customer's media pipeline rather than a one-off task declaration.
tests.evidence: ## Review checklist ... - [ ] Step 1: Acquire and validate pricing data ... - [ ] Step 5: Evaluate cost levers per service

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive, explicit list of gotchas/pitfalls specific to this domain in the misestimation checklist and inline notes (e.g., MaxBitrate not a cost lever, H.264 framerate trap, Router protocol gaps).
tests.evidence: MediaConnect MaxBitrate NOT presented as a TS cost lever (flat rate) ... H.264 outputs checked for INITIALIZE_FROM_SOURCE framerate control
